remaining_questions.question: I can't settle the number of vavs, and I don't agree with the primary reader's ONE. Reading the letters one by one, right to left, I see: shuruq vav, mem with hiriq, a complete tsadi with shva below, then TWO separate upright vav strokes, then tav and a period. I compared the tsadi with others in the same type and size: יִצְחָק in line10 and מִצְרַֽיִם in band1. In those words the tsadi's left arm does not look like an extra upright. Here, the space between mem and tav looks wider than tsadi plus one vav. I see the same thing at three scales: band3, band4/line23, and the full s292.jpg. That suggests וּמִצְווֹת. But I can't tell whether the holam dot sits over the first or the second vav, so I can't give an exact replacement string, and I haven't made a patch. A human needs to check the native pixels between the tsadi and the tav: is there one vav or two, and if two, which vav carries the holam?

verdict: I checked every s292 block against all four wide bands and the full native page, and checked the doubtful lines (10, 16, 17, 21–24) in the corrected full-height crops. I did not read the other lines-full crops (1–9, 11–15, 18–20) one by one; those lines were checked in the bands, where each line is fully visible in at least one band. Consonants, maqafs, punctuation and pointing match the candidate everywhere except possibly וּמִצְוֹת. I confirmed these points: כִסֵּא has no dagesh in the kaf; the final kaf of מִמֶּךָּ has a dagesh; in שֶׁתְּחָנֵּנוּ the first nun has a dagesh and the second does not; human422/423/426/427 are applied correctly. No meteg or low point was hidden. I made no patches. There is one open dispute: the vav count in וּמִצְוֹת (attah_nigleta, line23). The images look more like two vavs to me, but I can't place the holam, so it stays a question and not a patch. I did not reread English s293 because this is not the 284/288 pair and it was fully checked earlier. Pointing approval is withheld until the וּמִצְוֹת question is settled.
